section_summary: This section combines wartime correspondence about payments for oil shipped to Japan with intelligence estimates of Japanese refining capacity, synthetic fuel production, petroleum stocks, and tanker needs. A January 1942 naval intelligence report appears in multiple copies and extracts, alongside later requests for better production figures. The section also includes records on alleged Soviet oil deliveries to Japan, a claimed cottonseed oil fuel process, and a British account of oil imports from Iran.

subfiles.title: Payment arrangements for petroleum exports from the Netherlands East Indies to Japan
subfiles.about: Points to a memorandum on releasing blocked Japanese balances to pay Standard-Vacuum Oil Company.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a conversation with George S. Walden and Mr. Singer about $557,000 due for prior oil business.

subfiles.title: Shipment of Snow White Petrolatum to Yokohama
subfiles.about: Points to a report on A. Z. Phillips's order for petrolatum through Petroleos Mexicanos.
subfiles.summary: The order was reportedly viewed as commercial, with no suspicion of reexport.

subfiles.title: Map of Japanese refineries and oil storage depots
subfiles.about: Points to a letter transmitting a map of Japanese refineries and oil storage depots.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a refinery and depot location map.

subfiles.title: Routing note on Mitsui oil payments
subfiles.about: Forwards a memorandum on balances Mitsui owed General Petroleum Company.
subfiles.summary: Routes Mr. Lowe's conversation with Mr. Fox for review.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Mr. Lowe about Mitsui oil debts
subfiles.about: Records license and remittance questions involving Mitsui and General Petroleum Company.
subfiles.summary: Mitsui sought a Tokyo remittance to pay licensed debts for earlier U.S. oil shipments; a separate $900,000 claim for oil used in Japan remained under consideration.

subfiles.title: Standard-Vacuum remittances from Yokohama
subfiles.about: Details sums due for oil imported before freezing regulations and asks about releasing remittances.
subfiles.summary: Walden describes $557,561 already remitted, further sums expected against earlier exchange contracts, and Japanese interest in licenses for future shipments.

subfiles.title: Forwarding report on the Japanese oil situation
subfiles.from: W. A. Heard, Office of Naval Intelligence
subfiles.about: Forwards an oil situation report for the British Ministry of Economic Warfare.
subfiles.summary: Heard cautions that the report's estimates rest on incomplete information.

subfiles.title: Japanese refining capacity and synthetic petroleum manufacture
subfiles.to: Liaison Officer; British Ministry of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: Estimates Japanese refinery capacity, aviation fuel inputs, synthetic fuel methods, and plant locations.
subfiles.summary: The report assesses crude refining, aviation gasoline base stock, tetraethyl lead, iso-octane, and lubricants. It describes coal carbonization, hydrogenation, synthesis, alcohol fuels, and Fushun oil shale. Tables list refineries, synthetic oil plants, and iso-octane capacity in Japan and its possessions; the report stresses incomplete data.

subfiles.title: Under Secretary liaison routing slip
subfiles.about: Appears to route the naval intelligence material.
subfiles.summary: Brief, partly illegible routing notation.

subfiles.title: Request for updated synthetic oil information
subfiles.about: Asks for naval intelligence details on Japanese synthetic and substitute oil.
subfiles.summary: Requests report 409-300 and updates for a British Ministry of Economic Warfare inquiry.

subfiles.title: Request to Naval Intelligence on Japanese oil
subfiles.about: Seeks information on Japanese synthetic oil output, coal, and German equipment supplies.
subfiles.summary: The British Ministry of Economic Warfare wants current and projected output and obstacles to Japanese synthetic oil development.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about Soviet estimates of Japanese synthetic petroleum
subfiles.about: Records discussion of asking the Soviet government for Japanese synthetic petroleum estimates.
subfiles.summary: Mr. Paul sought Soviet figures despite doubts about their reliability and likely delay. Mr. Ballantine cited a British Embassy report and naval intelligence estimate, then drafted a telegram.

subfiles.title: Request for Soviet estimate of Japanese synthetic petroleum
subfiles.about: Asks the embassy to seek a Soviet production estimate.
subfiles.summary: Requests Soviet estimates for synthetic petroleum in Japan and Japanese-controlled territory.

subfiles.title: Copy of Naval Intelligence forwarding memorandum
subfiles.from: W. A. Heard, Office of Naval Intelligence
subfiles.about: Forwards the Japanese oil situation report.
subfiles.summary: Copy of the forwarding memorandum, noting incomplete source data.

subfiles.title: Copy of Japanese oil situation report
subfiles.about: Provides another copy of the naval report on Japanese refining and synthetic oil.
subfiles.summary: This copy repeats the discussion of aviation gasoline inputs, coal based synthetic fuel, oil shale, and substitutes. It includes tables of refinery, synthetic oil, and iso-octane plant locations and estimated capacities.

subfiles.title: Digest of Japanese oil situation report and appended tables
subfiles.about: Summarizes key estimates in the naval report and reproduces its production tables.
subfiles.summary: The digest highlights refining and aviation fuel bottlenecks, possible accumulated stocks, and an estimated 8.613 million barrels of annual synthetic oil plant capacity. It notes gaps concerning natural crude production and appends refinery, synthetic oil, and iso-octane tables.

subfiles.title: Japanese oil position: summary of Thornburg estimates
subfiles.about: Summarizes estimates of Japanese oil consumption, stocks, occupied production, refining, and tankers.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum estimates annual wartime consumption at 49.389 million barrels and reserves at 56 million barrels at the end of 1941. It argues that restored Netherlands East Indies and Borneo oil production and refineries, together with tanker transport, could support a prolonged Japanese war.

subfiles.title: Economic Warfare reports on tankers and refineries
subfiles.about: Points to reports on Japanese refineries and enemy-controlled tankers.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Economic Warfare intelligence reports.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about C. E. Meyer's Japanese oil information
subfiles.from: London, for the Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: Requests results of interviews with a former Standard-Vacuum manager in Japan.
subfiles.summary: London asks whether intelligence agencies have interviewed C. E. Meyer and seeks his information for the Hartley Sub-Committee's Japanese oil review.

subfiles.title: Reply to Senator Maloney on alleged Soviet oil deliveries
subfiles.about: Responds to a rumor that Soviet lend-lease petroleum was diverted to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Hull encloses his letter to Stettinius and says Soviet assurances have been received.

subfiles.title: Assurance to Stettinius on Soviet lend-lease shipments
subfiles.about: Addresses the allegation that Soviet petroleum shipments reached Japan.
subfiles.summary: Hull says inquiries found no reason to believe the report and raises no objection to continued Pacific route shipments.

subfiles.title: Senator Maloney's inquiry about Soviet oil supplies to Japan
subfiles.about: Asks whether Russia was supplying Japan with U.S. lend-lease petroleum products.
subfiles.summary: Maloney seeks evidence on the allegation and asks whether Soviet assurances were requested.

subfiles.title: Stettinius acknowledgment to Hull
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Hull's response concerning Senator Maloney's inquiry.
subfiles.summary: Stettinius says a reply has been sent to Maloney.

subfiles.title: U.S. petroleum exports to Japan as shares of U.S. consumption
subfiles.about: Compares U.S. petroleum exports to Japan from 1931 to 1941 with U.S. consumption.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum translates export shares into days of U.S. consumption for selected years. Its table gives annual percentages for crude petroleum, gasoline, kerosene, fuel oil, and lubricating oil.

subfiles.title: Senator Maloney thanks Hull
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the reply to his inquiry about alleged Soviet petroleum deliveries.
subfiles.summary: Maloney thanks Hull for answering his December inquiry.

subfiles.title: Bern report on Japanese coal-to-oil plants
subfiles.to: Secretary of State; Rayner, Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: Reports capacities and processes for selected Japanese and Manchurian synthetic oil plants.
subfiles.summary: The telegram lists reported Fischer and hydrogenation plants at Fushun, Ōmuta, Agochi, and Shiheigai and estimates total coal oil output at one billion liters.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Bern synthetic oil telegram
subfiles.to: Secretary of State; Rayner, Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: Paraphrases the Bern report on synthetic oil plants.
subfiles.summary: Repeats plant descriptions, capacities, and the one billion liter production estimate.

subfiles.title: Corrected paraphrase of Bern synthetic oil telegram
subfiles.to: Secretary of State; Rayner, Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: Corrects the paraphrase of reported Japanese and Manchurian coal-to-oil plants.
subfiles.summary: Gives corrected organization names and plant descriptions while retaining the one billion liter estimate.

subfiles.title: Challenge to Bern coal-to-oil estimate
subfiles.about: Asks for the source of the one billion liter synthetic oil estimate.
subfiles.summary: Barry notes similarities to a 1938 article and questions extrapolation from five plants.

subfiles.title: Draft query on Bern coal-to-oil estimate
subfiles.about: Drafts a request to verify the source and total synthetic oil estimate.
subfiles.summary: Questions extrapolation from five plants to an industry of more than thirty.

subfiles.title: Claimed gasoline production from cottonseed oil
subfiles.from: George Atcheson Jr., American Embassy, Chungking
subfiles.about: Forwards a French press claim of a Japanese cottonseed oil fuel process.
subfiles.summary: The despatch relays a report that Mr. Hibi produced crude oil and gasoline from refined cottonseed oil at Nantong.

subfiles.title: Copy of despatch on cottonseed oil fuel
subfiles.from: George Atcheson Jr., American Embassy, Chungking
subfiles.about: Repeats the reported Japanese cottonseed oil fuel discovery.
subfiles.summary: Copy of the despatch conveying Mr. Hibi's claimed process.

subfiles.title: Request for Soviet figures on Japanese petroleum
subfiles.about: Seeks detailed 1942–1943 Japanese petroleum production, refining, import, and consumption figures.
subfiles.summary: Requests figures for Sakhalin supplies, synthetic and shale oil, domestic crude, refining capacity, Netherlands East Indies production, and fuel consumption.

subfiles.title: Demolition of oil fields and refineries in the Netherlands East Indies
subfiles.about: Points to reports on demolition of oil facilities in the Netherlands East Indies and South Sumatra.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to two reports received from the Netherlands Embassy.

subfiles.title: British Embassy letter on Persian Gulf oil exports to Japan
subfiles.about: Sends a statement on the Persian Gulf share of oil exports to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Transmits the requested statement and import table.

subfiles.title: Oil for Japan: Anglo-Iranian sales and import table
subfiles.about: Explains Anglo-Iranian crude sales to Japan and compares Japan-Manchukuo oil imports by source.
subfiles.summary: The statement says a twelve-cargo Abadan contract had yielded only 278,000 barrels and explains the company's royalty pressures in Iran. A table lists 1937–1940 imports from the United States, Netherlands East Indies, Sakhalin, Persian Gulf, and other sources, with notes on ownership and sources.

subfiles.title: Report on Japan's oil transport fleet
subfiles.from: Carl H. Boehringer, American Embassy, Chungking
subfiles.about: Transmits a Netherlands intelligence report on Japanese tanker tonnage and losses.
subfiles.summary: Boehringer sends a report covering tanker statistics through January 1944.
